name: Pursed-Lip Breathing

instructions.description: Sit comfortably on the floor or in a chair, depending on your preference. Maintain an upright and relaxed posture, with your neck and shoulders relaxed throughout the exercise.
Inhale gently through your nose with your mouth closed. Breathe in slowly and naturally for about two seconds. There is no need to take a deep breath. Allow your belly to gently expand as you inhale.

Exhale slowly through gently pursed lips, as if you were blowing on a hot drink or gently whistling. Breathe out slowly and steadily for four or more seconds. Allow your belly to gently draw back toward your spine as you exhale.
Return to normal breathing whenever needed.

TIPS: 
Pursed-lip breathing may feel awkward or uncomfortable at first. With regular practice, it gets easier. These tips can help, too:

- Try putting your hands on your belly to feel it moving in and out as you breathe.
- Always breathe out for longer than you breathe in.
- Breathe slowly and easily — in and out — until you’re able to control your breathing.
- Don’t force the air out of your lungs.

performanceMetrics.notes: Record the time performed with comfortable, controlled technique.
Record a comfortable breathing rate without prescribing a universal norm.

commentsNotes: In Step 5, I have included some tips for the exercise. It would be useful to add a sort of ‘Tips’ box to the exercises, where tips such as those described in Step 5 could be included.

variations.variationDescription: Pursed-Lip Breathing — Shorter Practice Version: Use a shorter comfortable practice period while preserving relaxed breathing.
